intent_synonyms: writing repudiation and vindication|never underestimate a poor youth|establishing a three-year challenge
model_instruction: Apply pressure before eruption; humiliation must become a long-term payoff promise.
summary: An opening based on repudiation or expulsion must first crush dignity, then delay retaliation into a long-term commitment.
details: This route sustains reading through suppression, an oath, further humiliation, and eventual payoff rather than an instant reversal. Establish shame and pressure, then an oath and first counterattack; do not compress both suffering and fulfillment into a one-chapter event log.
pacing_strategy: Deliver the first effective counterattack within three chapters
pitfalls: weak ending to vindication|supporting characters retaliate before the protagonist can deliver

intent_synonyms: writing rules horror|writing zoo rules|consequences of breaking rules
model_instruction: Establish binding rules first, then progressively reveal costs and loopholes.
summary: Build clear rules and let characters gain information by alternating compliance, testing, and violation.
details: Satisfaction comes from deciphering and exploiting rules, not arbitrary trespassing. Establish rules, anomalous signs, and testing costs in the zoo, then show consequences and solutions after a limited violation.
pacing_strategy: Establish rules before solving the predicament
pitfalls: rules are mere scenery|punishment has no cost|mystery revealed too early

keywords: suppression then eruption|rise after setbacks|patient endurance
intent_synonyms: writing pressure before release|writing emotional eruption|arranging pent-up tension
model_instruction: Make suppression concrete and make the eruption change the situation.
summary: Accumulate restrictions, losses, and concessions, then deliver concentrated release at an unavoidable breaking point.
details: The opening makes readers share restraint; the later section changes relationships, circumstances, or rules in one stroke. Make losses tangible and fulfillment decisive instead of relying on slogans or emotional adjectives.
core_tone: Pent-up pressure followed by strong payoff
pacing_strategy: Accumulate restrictions to a critical point before eruption
pitfalls: no real prior suppression|eruption changes nothing|immediate reset afterward

keywords: urban son-in-law comeback|live-in son-in-law|scorned husband|urban son-in-law system
intent_synonyms: writing son-in-law fiction|a humiliated husband's turnaround|son-in-law vindication|urban son-in-law system story
model_instruction: Apply pressure first and deliver concentrated payoff after humiliation accumulates.
summary: Establish low status and wounded dignity through the spouse's family's humiliation, coldness, and contempt before revealing identity or strength for vindication.
details: The core is status disparity and its later reversal. Quickly establish the protagonist's low position through repeated humiliation by parents-in-law and relatives, then retaliate through a concealed identity or business strategy. Do not make the protagonist dominant from the start; endurance must precede release.
genre_aliases: son-in-law comeback;live-in son-in-law;scorned husband's turnaround;urban son-in-law
pacing_strategy: Establish clear status disparity within three chapters
pitfalls: protagonist dominant immediately|counterattack too early|no convincing humiliation

keywords: grovel romance|angsty romance|pain before sweetness|wealthy-family romance|regretful pursuit
intent_synonyms: writing grovel romance|male lead's remorse|pacing angst|wealthy-family reconciliation
model_instruction: Begin with emotional injury and later remorse; emotional reversal must carry a cost.
summary: Make the male lead's harm specific and substantial enough to justify the heroine's pain and decisive departure, then sustain tension through remorse and restitution.
details: Credibility depends on concrete indifference, misunderstanding, or injury and a well-motivated departure. Later regret must appear in costly action rather than speeches. Avoid easy forgiveness; any softening needs a convincing process.
genre_aliases: grovel romance;angsty romance;pain before sweetness;regretful male lead;wealthy-family reconciliation
pacing_strategy: Make early injuries real and later repentance costly
pitfalls: initial harm lacks weight|heroine forgives too quickly|repentance costs nothing

keywords: Fanqie-style power fantasy|fast-paced male-audience serial|Fanqie style
intent_synonyms: writing Fanqie-style payoffs|fast vindication|Fanqie narrative style
model_instruction: Use fast, dense pacing with a payoff every three chapters.
summary: This platform-specific style calls for very fast, dense narration: a small payoff every 200-300 words, a major payoff every three to five chapters, and immediate opening conflict.
details: Introduce conflict within the first three sentences and complete initial vindication or reversal within three chapters. A strong special advantage should work through strategy, subverted expectations, or information gaps rather than thoughtless domination. Avoid protracted setup and long introspection; give dialogue subtext and internet humor.
genre_aliases: fast male-audience serial;Fanqie style;high-density power fantasy
pacing_strategy: A major payoff every three chapters and at least one small payoff each chapter
pitfalls: sluggish pacing|sparse payoffs|overlong setup|flat dialogue

keywords: Zhihu-style short fiction|first-person short fiction|Zhihu style|contemporary short romance|short-story reversal
intent_synonyms: writing Zhihu shorts|writing first person|Zhihu style|paid Zhihu short fiction
model_instruction: Use immersive first person, an explosive opening, and precise cliffhangers.
summary: This platform-specific short-fiction route uses first person, a gripping opening within 50 words, fast progression, strong conflict, and precisely placed paid-section breakpoints.
details: Hook readers through conflict or suspense within 50 words. Use one-sentence paragraphs, fewer conversations and more internal monologue, several reversals, and breakpoints at emotional or suspense peaks. For this route, avoid third person, slow-burn setup, and lengthy environmental description.
genre_aliases: first-person short fiction;Zhihu style;Zhihu premium shorts
core_tone: Immersive first person with fast pacing
pacing_strategy: Explosive opening within 50 words and precisely placed breakpoints
pitfalls: third-person narration|slow opening|poorly placed breakpoint|too few reversals

keywords: mini-app short fiction|paid short fiction|mini-app style|paid mini-app story
intent_synonyms: writing mini-app shorts|designing paid-section cliffhangers|short-story pacing|paid mini-app fiction
model_instruction: Use strong emotional conflict, frequent painful beats, and precisely placed paid-section cliffhangers.
summary: This platform-specific route places three mildly unsettling events in the first 500 words and a major shock around 3,000 words, using emotional tension to encourage continued paid reading.
details: Accumulate unease and anger through small conflicts, placing the paywall at an emotional peak. Morally wrong but legal mistreatment can create identification. Leave suspense or unresolved conflict at the end; avoid a flat opening or resolving everything immediately after the paywall, while preserving continued appeal.
genre_aliases: paid short fiction;mini-app style;emotional short fiction;mini-app short fiction
core_tone: Strong emotional conflict and frequent anguish
pacing_strategy: Three small conflicts within 500 words and one major conflict around 3,000 words
pitfalls: flat opening|poor paid breakpoint|instant total resolution after payment|insufficient emotional buildup

keywords: transmigration|entering a novel|otherworld transfer|historical bureaucracy|court intrigue
intent_synonyms: writing transmigration|novel-entry openings|modern-knowledge advantage|historical official intrigue
model_instruction: Establish the period gap and survival pressure before turning information advantages into tangible gains.
summary: Resolve identity and period constraints first, then use knowledge differences to change the situation.
details: Transmigration is not an omnipotent cheat. Establish identity replacement, speech habits, social rules, and survival risks; modern knowledge pays off only with suitable technical conditions. Do not change institutions by declaration or make every historical character foolish.
genre_aliases: transmigration;entering a novel;otherworld restart;historical intrigue;bureaucratic fiction
core_tone: Identity disparity followed by information-based payoff
pacing_strategy: Adapt to rules before achieving a local breakthrough
pitfalls: modern knowledge works unconditionally|historical people collectively foolish|identity inconsistencies never questioned

intent_synonyms: writing urban superpowers|modern high-power martial fiction|ability awakening
model_instruction: Keep supernatural conflict constrained by modern order, and attach costs to ability payoffs.
summary: Preserve both modern social constraints and supernatural satisfaction rather than turning the city into reskinned cultivation fantasy.
details: Define ability limits, costs, exposure risk, and governing institutions. Powerful combat must affect identity, resources, or relationships. Avoid unlimited upgrades or public battles without accountability.
core_tone: Extraordinary power contrasted with modern order
pacing_strategy: Show ability costs and a first practical confrontation within three chapters
pitfalls: cost-free abilities|modern institutions disappear|combat has no aftermath

intent_synonyms: writing cultivation|writing sects|writing heavenly tribulation
model_instruction: Establish karmic and realm constraints first; breakthroughs require resources, inner growth, or costs.
summary: Use power realms, sects, karmic consequences, and resource competition to create a durable order.
details: Cultivation is not a list of realm names. Each breakthrough should consume resources, change mindset, create lineage pressure, or risk tribulation. Sect relations should govern distribution and opposing positions. Avoid seclusion diaries and unprepared enlightenment.
pacing_strategy: Compress routine training and deliver strong magical-contest payoffs
pitfalls: cost-free realm breakthrough|seclusion diary|karmic rules stop functioning

intent_synonyms: writing apocalypse|zombie siege|wasteland survival|science-fiction survival base
model_instruction: Resource pressure precedes heroic display, and survival choices must leave costs.
summary: Maintain pressure through resources, trust, and safe zones.
details: Satisfaction comes from hard choices under extreme resource constraints, not unconditional protagonist cheats. Water, medicine, food, ammunition, and shelters must become plot variables. Do not omit hunger or keep team relations permanently harmonious.
pacing_strategy: Keep crises coming while each reshapes the resource situation
pitfalls: unlimited resources|apocalypse without pressure|crises measured only by monster count

intent_synonyms: writing sweet romance|writing school romance|writing attraction
model_instruction: Use low conflict and rich interaction; tender payoffs must arise from concrete behavior rather than labels.
summary: Everyday interaction, detailed care, and resolved misunderstandings should provide steady emotional rewards.
details: Build warmth through actions, choices, favoritism, jealousy, protection, and shared secrets, keeping conflicts small and specific. Avoid manufactured sweetness and characters who only blush or feel racing hearts.
pacing_strategy: At least one perceptible tender beat or relationship advance per chapter
pitfalls: artificial sweetness|only blushing and heartbeats|misunderstandings drag too long

intent_synonyms: writing deductions|criminal case plotting|planting clues
model_instruction: Keep clues fair while delaying interpretation; truth must connect back to earlier evidence.
summary: Connect clues, misdirection, suspect motives, and revelation order into a coherent whole.
details: Distinguish facts, character inferences, and authorial misdirection. Evidence should be findable on rereading; reversals must reinterpret previously shown information. Avoid new evidence from nowhere or a detective solving cases through revelation.
pacing_strategy: Each investigation round advances one true lead and one false lead
pitfalls: evidence appears from nowhere|detective revelation|hollow suspect motives

intent_synonyms: writing farming fiction|business management fiction|infrastructure fiction
model_instruction: Favor accumulation over frequent explosions; intermediate achievements must be visible and usable.
summary: Resource cycles, productive efficiency, and growing communities create sustained satisfaction.
details: Do not merely log daily activities. Give each stage a production goal, resource bottleneck, solution, and visible result; let relationships support community expansion. Avoid ledger-like numbers and obstacle-free wealth.
pacing_strategy: Frequent small-goal payoffs and volume-end resolution of major goals
pitfalls: daily-log management|invisible results|no resource bottleneck

intent_synonyms: writing entertainment fiction|celebrity career arcs|variety-show fiction
model_instruction: Make career and emotional arcs create difficult choices for one another.
summary: Use competition for opportunities, public-opinion reversals, and creative achievements to carry payoffs.
details: Do not rely solely on romance and trending topics. Characters need goals involving productions, performances, auditions, endorsements, or awards. Opinion reversals require evidence and a dissemination path. Avoid omnipotent trending lists and stagnant careers.
pacing_strategy: Each short arc produces a creative-work result or public-opinion outcome
pitfalls: trending lists solve everything|hollow creative achievements|unconvincing fandom dynamics

intent_synonyms: writing esports|writing matches|writing teamwork
model_instruction: Keep competitive goals clear; victory and defeat arise from strategy, execution, and teamwork.
summary: Make rules, game versions, lineups, mechanics, and psychological play form an understandable causal chain to victory or defeat.
details: Excitement requires readers to understand disadvantage, tactical choices, key execution, and team coordination. Prepare outcomes rather than deciding them through slogans; do not leave mechanics vague.
pacing_strategy: Strong match pacing and brief training payoffs
pitfalls: unclear mechanics|victory through slogans|teamwork lacks causality

intent_synonyms: writing cosmic horror|creating uncanny mystery|writing sanity costs
model_instruction: Keep boundaries around the unknown; fear comes from insufficient information and escalating costs.
summary: Use cognitive limits, anomalous details, and irreversible consequences to create pressure.
details: Cosmic horror is not a pile of tentacles. Every approach to truth should cost security, relationships, sanity, or identity; excessive explanation weakens fear. Avoid monster-catalog exposition and effortless comprehension of higher beings.
pacing_strategy: Anomalies first, evidence next, limited explanation last
pitfalls: monster instruction manual|higher beings made trivial|no sanity cost

intent_synonyms: writing academy fiction|entrance assessments|competition among peers
model_instruction: Use clearly regulated peer competition, with growth demonstrated through examinations and rankings.
summary: Build a growth ladder through institutions, cohort relationships, mentor resources, and staged assessments.
details: The academy must affect events: courses, clubs, assessments, rankings, and mentor choices change resource distribution. Make growth visible under peer pressure. Avoid empty institutions and classmates who exist only to watch.
pacing_strategy: Demonstrate each stage's change through an assessment or ranking
pitfalls: hollow academy rules|all peers made foolish|mentors merely serve as cheats

intent_synonyms: writing scenario arcs|designing levels|writing scenario rewards
model_instruction: Establish rules, goals, costs, and rewards together.
summary: Give each scenario independent rules and completion goals while advancing growth in the main plot.
details: A scenario is not a random map. Clarify entry conditions, failure costs, hidden rules, reward mechanisms, and main-story connections. Completion must bring change back into the outside world. Avoid unrelated scenarios or arbitrary rewards.
pacing_strategy: At least one exploitation or reversal of a rule in each scenario
pitfalls: scenario disconnected from main plot|vague completion goal|rewards without cost

keywords: western fantasy adventure|magic and knights|otherworld adventure
intent_synonyms: writing western fantasy|writing magic systems|knightly adventures
model_instruction: Establish world rules before spectacle; adventures must change faction relationships and costs.
summary: Support epic scope through magic rules, species positions, travel goals, and faction conflict.
details: Do not merely accumulate names. Magic, gods, peoples, monarchy, and adventure goals should constrain one another. Each victory should alter territory, factions, or religious relationships. Avoid reskinned cultivation fiction and omnipotent magic.
pacing_strategy: Adventure delivers spectacle at a cost
pitfalls: omnipotent magic|species are decorative|adventures do not change the world

keywords: historical-romance intrigue|palace and household rivalry|legitimacy conflict
intent_synonyms: writing historical romance|palace intrigue|household intrigue
model_instruction: Let ritual law and status constrain conflict; outcomes come from planning and countermeasures within the rules.
summary: Treat identity, etiquette, family resources, and reputational consequences as real constraints.
details: Historical romance is not modern people in old clothing. Speech and action must reflect ritual, family, class, and reputation; counterattacks require evidence, social obligations, and rules. Avoid modern slang and a heroine confronting every institution without cost.
pacing_strategy: Build evidence during suppression and establish legitimacy during retaliation
pitfalls: modern slang|intrigue without evidence|ritual constraints disappear

intent_synonyms: writing fantasy romance|immortal romance|creating a sense of destiny
model_instruction: Make romance and power arcs pressure one another; destiny must not replace choice.
summary: Bring emotional choices, cultivation costs, and world rules into the same conflict.
details: Do not write advancement and romance as unrelated tracks. Emotional progress must affect cultivation, factions, identity, or world rules; painful beats need costly choices. Avoid all-solving destiny and a male lead taking over the heroine's growth.
core_tone: Emotional choices bound to power costs
pacing_strategy: Every emotional turn changes a position or ability
pitfalls: romance disconnected from main plot|destiny replaces action|heroine's growth outsourced to the male lead

keywords: period fiction|Republican-era romance|modern historical fiction|courtyard community|factory ration coupons
intent_synonyms: writing period fiction|Republican-era love stories|creating period atmosphere|courtyard and factory fiction
model_instruction: Material conditions and social relationships of the period are the primary constraints.
summary: Build authenticity through prices, occupations, family structures, and historical risks.
details: A date label is not enough. Food, clothing, housing, transport, workplace institutions, kinship, war, or policy pressure must affect choices. Ground romance and careers in their period rather than importing modern consumer assumptions unchanged.
genre_aliases: period fiction;Republican-era romance;modern history;courtyard community;factory fiction
core_tone: Emotion and survival under period constraints
pacing_strategy: Everyday detail sustains realism; key milestones deliver historical shocks
pitfalls: decorative historical background|modern values imposed mechanically|implausible material conditions

keywords: quick-transmigration missions|relationship mission system|world hopping|original host
intent_synonyms: writing quick transmigration|relationship-target missions|small worlds|missions involving an original host
model_instruction: Advance mission objectives and character emotion together; completion cannot rely only on foreknowledge.
summary: Give each world a clear mission, restrictions, emotional variables, and value for the overarching plot.
details: Do not repeat vindication with new scenery. Each world needs its own theme and central relationship; mission limits must force difficult choices, and rewards must advance overarching identity or memory. Avoid repeated world templates and systems that provide answers directly.
genre_aliases: relationship mission system;small worlds;world-hopping missions;mission agent;original host
pacing_strategy: Set goals at arrival, add restrictions in the middle, and reconnect to the main arc at the end
pitfalls: repeated worlds|system replaces thinking|rewards have no main-plot value

intent_synonyms: writing fanfiction|writing derivative fiction|writing canon characters|controlling out-of-character behavior
model_instruction: Respect recognizable canon features; rewrites need clear differences and costs.
summary: Keep recognizable tension between canon characterization, world rules, and new variables.
details: Do not merely borrow names. Preserve recognizable motives, relationships, and ability limits; explain divergence points and butterfly effects in the new main plot. Avoid making every canon character unrecognizable or simply retelling canon events.
pacing_strategy: Stabilize canon anchors before expanding divergence consequences
pitfalls: out-of-character behavior|retelling canon|new variables have no butterfly effects
